In addition, the crystal structures of sevoflurane, (CF3)2CHOCH3, (CF3)2CHOCHF2, (CF3)2CHOCF3, and (CF3)2CFOCF3 were determined by x-ray diffraction, providing a detailed insight into trends of the bond parameters and the intermolecular interactions in the solid state. The interpretation of the bond parameters is supported by calculated values (density functional theory, DFT).

item.title: FLP Mediated Conversion of Difluorobenzylalkynes to Fluoroallenyl Oniums via an SN1’ Pathway
item.description:
Frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) selective C‒F activation of difluorobenzylalkynes allows the formation of fluoroallenic oniums via an SN1’ substitution pathway. The fluoroallenic onium salts are synthetic precursors that allow subsequent functionalization at allenic and onium positions.


ABSTRACT

Fluoroallenes represent an attractive class of synthons and are congeners to naturally occurring haloallenes, yet their preparation remains challenging. We report that frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) mediated selective monodefluorination of difluorobenzylalkynes generates geminal fluorobenzylalkyne onium salts as kinetic products, which subsequently isomerize into thermodynamically preferred fluoroallenyl onium salts through an SN1′pathway. The onium-stabilized fluoroallenes can undergo further derivatization at both allenic and onium positions, providing modular access to new fluorocarbon architectures.

item.title: The Terphenyl Phosphines as Effective and Affordable Ligands for Pd‐Catalyzed Arylation of Secondary Aliphatic Amines
item.description:
TRuPhos, a terphenyl phosphine ligand, enables highly efficient Pd-catalyzed C─N coupling of secondary aliphatic amines. With only 0.1–5 mol% catalyst, a broad range of cyclic, acyclic, and α-branched secondary amines couple with (hetero)aryl halides, even base-sensitive five-membered heteroarenes. Mechanistic studies reveal the key transmetalation pathways.


ABSTRACT

This study investigates the performance of terphenyl phosphine palladium catalyst precursors in C–N coupling reactions of secondary aliphatic amines. The TRuPhos-based palladium catalyst precursor has been found to be highly efficient, combined with NaOTMS as base, especially for the C─N coupling of five-membered heteroaryl halides with cyclic secondary aliphatic amines (including α-branched, sterically hindered amines) as well as acyclic aliphatic amines. Replacing the 2,6‑isopropyl groups on the non‑phosphorus‑containing phenyl ring with sterically less demanding isopropoxy groups is a key reason why TRuPhos is highly efficient for the C─N coupling of bulky secondary aliphatic amines, whereas the presence or absence of an isopropyl group at the 4‑position of this phenyl ring has little effect on the catalytic performance. Mechanistic studies reveal that with NaOTMS as the base, the transmetalation pathway most likely proceeds via the intermediate [(TRuPhos)(Ar)PdII(OTMS)], formed from the oxidative addition product and the base, which then reacts with the amine to yield the amido complex [(TRuPhos)(Ar)PdII(NR1R2)], although a direct metalation pathway between the oxidative addition product and the amide anion as strong base NaOtBu used, and a pathway through the adduct [(TRuPhos)(Ar)PdIIX(HNR1R2)] of the oxidative addition product to amine having less sterically hindered cyclic amines cannot be ruled out.

item.title: Introduction of a Double‐Headed Nucleotide Into G‐Quadruplex DNA: Position‐Dependent Stabilization and Structural Insights
item.description:
A double-headed bis-guanine (G) nucleotide (GG) was evaluated as a noncanonical building block in G-quadruplexes (G4s). Biophysical and computational analyses reveal that GG can directly participate in G-tetrads and strongly stabilize G4s in a position- and topology-dependent manner. These findings establish design rules for using GG to engineer highly stable G4-based oligonucleotides (ONs) and aptamers.


ABSTRACT

G-quadruplexes are structurally diverse nucleic acid motifs with important biological properties as well as emerging applications in biotechnology and therapeutics. Here, we investigate whether a double-headed bis-guanine (G) nucleotide, GG—a substantial deviation from canonical nucleic acid architecture—can be accommodated within G-quadruplex structures and how its effects depend on sequence context and topology. Using a combination of circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy, thermal denaturation analysis, UV thermal differential spectroscopy (TDS), fluorescence light-up assays, polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE) analysis, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we show that GG can substitute two consecutive guanosines in G-quadruplex-forming oligonucleotides (ONs) and directly participate in G-tetrad formation, but with strong sequence- and position-dependent consequences. GG incorporation is best tolerated in parallel G-quadruplexes and at G-tetrad steps with low native torsional twist, where local unwinding can be accommodated. In a tetramolecular TG4T system, GG positioned near the 3’-end of the G-stack preserved parallel G-quadruplex topology while providing significant thermal stabilization (+21°C). In the antiparallel thrombin-binding aptamer (TBA), a single GG incorporation yielded exceptional stabilization (+34°C) but was accompanied by altered topological signatures. Together, the results presented herein establish GG as a powerful but context-dependent G-quadruplex stabilizer and define design principles for its use in engineered G-quadruplexes and aptamer development.

item.title: Benzo[c][1,2,5]Thiadiazole Linkers Enhance the Effectiveness of Cavity‐Containing Supramolecular Photocatalysts
item.description:
Seven novel supramolecular photosensitizers based on benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole (BTZ) tethered to calix[4]arene (C[4]) scaffolds are reported with facile, scalable, and selective syntheses. Their abilities to produce singlet oxygen have been tested through the photo-oxidation of α-terpinene. Probing for different structural and electronic features, outstanding performance was observed for the catalyst with two C[4] cavities proximal to BTZ, providing an impressive eightfold enhancement in reactivity compared to its non-cavity-containing analogue.


ABSTRACT

A family of seven novel supramolecular photosensitizers comprising benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole (BTZ) tethered calix[4]arene (C[4]) scaffolds has been synthesized using cross-coupling strategies with selectively halogenated C[4]s, affording target compounds in high yield using facile purification. Their respective abilities to produce singlet oxygen has been evaluated through the photo-oxidation of α-terpinene, and structure–activity relationships established, probing factors such as cavity:photosensitizer ratio, distance of cavity to photosensitizer linker, and steric hindrance around the upper-rim of the cavity. The presence of two C[4] cavities proximal to the photosensitizing BTZ unit provided vastly increased effectiveness in enhancing effective concentration through host:guest interactions, resulting in an eightfold increase in efficiency for the best-performing member of the compound library benchmarked against a small-molecule analogue, and reaching reaction completion in 1 h at 2.5 mol% loading. In contrast, systematically increasing the cavity:photosensitizing linker distance led to a reduction in improvement to 1.1-fold relative to the small molecule analogue, confirming that these factors are pivotal in designing a suitable system based on the guest substrate.

item.title: Dioxygen Reduction at a Cu(I) Complex Supported by a Macrocyclic N3O Ligand System
item.description:
A non-reactive [CuI(14-TMC)]+ complex is transformed to an efficient catalyst [CuI(14-TMCO)]+ (TMCO = 4,8,12-trimethyl-1-oxa-4,8,12-triazacyclotetradecane) for 4e−/4H+ reduction of O2 by N → O substitution.


ABSTRACT

CuI(14 TMCO) (1), involving a N3O-macrocycle, reacts with O2 at cryogenic temperatures to yield an end-on peroxodicopper(II) species. The N4-analogue CuI(14-TMC) (2) remains unreactive under similar conditions. 2 contains an average short Cu─N bond length, resulting in a dominating trans-effect, which inhibits O2 binding. In contrast, an elongated Cu─OTMCO bond trans to the O2-binding site in 1 allows O2-coordination. The catalytic reduction of O2 to H2O undergoes a full 4e−/4H+ process in 1. Notably, [CuI(12-TMC)]+ (3), involving a smaller N4-macrocycle where the Cu(I) ion is forced to move out of the plane formed by the four nitrogen atoms, also binds O2. However, in contrast to 1, 3 mediates the catalytic 2e−/2H+ reduction of O2 to H2O2 via two ligand-assisted protonation steps. In this case, the reduction of O2 involves the initial formation of a side-on peroxodicopper(II) species, where the weak Cu─Operoxo bond distance resulting from the strong σ-donation from the trans Cu─N bond presumably leads to the release of H2O2 upon protonation. The present study provides deep mechanistic insights into the transition metal-mediated O2 reduction process and reveals how the first coordination sphere can be tuned to control the 2e−/2H+ versus 4e−/4H+ reductions of O2.

item.title: A Stable Isopterin Mimic of a Potent Bacterial Stimulant of T Cells
item.description:
A microbial metabolite covalently binds immunological protein MR1 to potently activate specific lymphocytes called MAIT cells, but it is too unstable for biological applications. Here, using synthesis, assays, protein crystallography, and computer modelling, we report a water-stable analogue that activates reporter cells expressing the MAIT T cell receptor and mimics the protein-bound conformation of the natural product, forming a basis for designing new immunotherapeutics.


ABSTRACT

Mucosal-associated invariant T cells (MAIT cells) are innate-like immune cells (T lymphocytes) that protect against bacterial infections. They are potently activated by the microbial metabolite 5-(2-oxopropylideneamino)-d-ribitylaminouracil (5-OP-RU), which bonds covalently to an amine of a specific lysine residue of the antigen-presenting protein MR1 to form an imine (Schiff base). However, 5-OP-RU undergoes rapid degradative intramolecular cyclisation in water, and more robust analogues are needed for therapeutic applications. Here, inspired by the structural similarities between 5-OP-RU and 6-formylpterin, a water-stable covalent MR1 ligand that does not activate MAIT cells, we describe the design and synthesis of a novel isopterin analogue of this microbial natural product, and show that it is both water-stable and activates reporter cells expressing the MAIT T cell receptor. Further, we present a protein-bound crystal structure and molecular dynamics simulations of this stable analogue to show that it mimics the MR1-bound conformation of 5-OP-RU. This study demonstrates the potential of this bicyclic scaffold for stabilising 5-OP-RU mimetics, advances our understanding of the molecular requirements for MR1 binding and MAIT cell activation, and informs the design and synthesis of future MAIT cell antigens as potential immunotherapeutics.

item.title: Electrochemical α‐Acyloxylation by Cooperative Chiral Amine and Proton Shuttle Catalysis via an Asymmetric SN1 Mechanism
item.description:
This work establishes an electrochemical strategy for asymmetric SN1 reactions through the generation of α-imino carbocations by aminocatalysis and anodic oxidation. An imidazole-based proton shuttle regulates proton transfer and promotes efficient hydrogen evolution at the cathode. ScopeMap-guided substrate selection systematically explores chemical space, while mechanistic studies reveal the key role of proton shuttling in catalytic turnover.


ABSTRACT

Asymmetric SN1 reactions offer a powerful approach to enantioenriched molecules but remain challenging in carbocation generation and proton manipulation. Herein, we report an electrochemical asymmetric α-acyloxylation of aldehydes through an α-imino carbocation intermediate generated by aminocatalysis and anodic oxidation. A catalytic imidazole derivative serves as a recyclable proton shuttle, facilitating cathodic hydrogen evolution. The reaction scope was systematically evaluated using a ScopeMap-guided substrate-selection strategy, enabling uniform sampling of the chemical space. Mechanistic studies support the crucial role of the proton shuttle in facilitating chemical transformation and the catalytic cycle.

item.title: Iron Alcoholate‐Derived FeOOH Nanoflowers Enabling Lattice Oxygen‐Mediated Oxygen Evolution
item.description:
This work reports a ligand-regulated solvothermal strategy to prepare iron-based metal alcoholate nanoflowers. Mixed ligands enable precise structural control, while solution etching introduces crystalline–amorphous coupling to enhance electrocatalytic performance. Operando characterizations confirm that the material reconstructs into active FeOOH phases during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), which proceeds via the lattice oxygen-mediated mechanism (LOM).


ABSTRACT

Although metal alcoholates have certain applications in the research of oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts, they still have problems of low stability and activity, which restrict their development. To address these issues, this work regulates the ratio of iron-based metal alcoholate ligands by the hydrothermal method and constructs nanoflower-like nanostructures with crystalline and amorphous coupling through etching, thereby improving the catalytic activity. Among them, Fe-gly-1.5 demonstrates exceptional catalytic performance under high current density, evidenced by a 243 mV overpotential (100 mA cm−2) and 200 h stability (250 mA cm−2). Moreover, the two-electrode alkaline water electrolyzer assembled with Fe-gly-1.5 and Pt/C catalysts shows sustainable stability in the overall water splitting process. Electrochemical studies using probe molecules such as TMAOH and methanol demonstrate that the mixed‑ligand system exhibits unique advantages in catalytic reactions. Further investigations through in situ Raman and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, combined with differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), reveal that the active phase of Fe-gly-1.5 is δ/β-FeOOH formed via reconstruction during the OER process, and confirm that its reaction pathway follows the lattice oxygen-mediated mechanism (LOM).

item.title: Lignin‐Derived Dual‐Dynamic Covalent Adaptable Networks: From Solubilization‐Enabled Fabrication to Recyclable Adhesives and Carbon Fiber Composites
item.description:
High-value utilization of lignin is achieved via a dynamic covalent chemistry strategy, by which high-performance and sustainable covalent adaptable networks are fabricated. These networks can be employed not only as high-strength adhesives with thermally reversible debonding capability but also as degradable matrices for carbon-fiber composites, enabling closed-loop recycling and promoting the development of the circular economy for polymeric materials.


ABSTRACT

Lignin, a renewable biomass-derived aromatic polymer, is restricted by poor solubility and low accessibility of its active functional groups, which hinders its application in high-performance materials. Herein, a dynamic covalent chemistry strategy was proposed: lignin was solubilized in 1,3-propanediol via hydrogen bonding, and lignin-based covalent adaptable networks (CANs) were fabricated through synergistic ring-opening esterification, thiol–anhydride reaction, and thiol–ene click reaction, integrating dual dynamic mechanisms (anhydride–hydroxyl transesterification and anhydride–thiol thioester exchange) for dynamic responsiveness. The optimal sample (L1P1MT1, anhydride:thiol = 1:1) exhibits excellent performance: as an adhesive, it achieves a shear strength of 11.8 MPa on steel with stable bonding over −40°C to 40°C and in complex media, plus thermal debonding at 130°C; as a matrix, carbon fiber composites prepared via vacuum-assisted resin infusion (VARI) show superior tensile properties and can be fully degraded in 1 M NaOH at 25°C within 7 h. Recycled carbon fibers retain their original structure and performance, enabling closed-loop recycling. This work realizes high-value lignin utilization, providing a green route toward high-performance, sustainable CANs with broad prospects in adhesives and advanced composites, thereby advancing green materials development and the polymer circular economy.

item.title: Chain‐Length‐Selective Aperture Closure of a Cobalt(III) Tris(Salen) Cryptophane With Bridging Diamines
item.description:
Chain-length-selective aperture closure of a cobalt(III) tris(salen) cryptophane is achieved by bridging diamines whose lengths match the Co⋯Co distance. The same closed-cage complexes are obtained both by direct diamine introduction and by ligand exchange from a preformed open-cage complex. This dual approach provides a new design principle for stimuli–responsive molecular containers.


ABSTRACT

Precise geometric matching between a bridging ligand and its target binding sites provides a powerful yet underexplored mechanism for selective structural control in supramolecular host systems. Here we demonstrate that the aperture of a cobalt(III) tris(salen) cryptophane can be selectively closed by bridging diamines whose chain length is geometrically compatible with the Co⋯Co distance within the cage framework. Systematic variation of the diamine chain length revealed pronounced chain-length selectivity, with efficient formation of a single closed-cage complex, LCo3(diamine)3(OTf)3, observed only for diamines of appropriate length. Diamines that were too short produced mixtures of incompletely bridged species, whereas longer diamines gave additional products containing diamines with monodentate coordination. Furthermore, the same closed-cage complexes were generated by ligand exchange from a preformed open-cage complex bearing monodentate methylamine ligands, demonstrating that aperture closure can also be achieved through dynamic structural transformation. These results establish geometric compatibility between bridging ligands and metal coordination sites as a design principle for chain-length-selective aperture closure in cryptophane-based hosts. Moreover, access to the same closed-cage complexes through ligand exchange provides a strategy for the dynamic modulation of molecular host architectures.

item.title: A Robust Mitochondria‐Targeted Photosensitizer Synergizes With Cisplatin Chemotherapy for Enhanced Antitumor Immunity
item.description:
A mitochondria-targeted photosensitizer, CMPE, has been developed to enable efficient reactive oxygen species generation for photo-induced antitumor immunotherapy. Under light irradiation, CMPE triggers mitochondrial oxidative stress and robust immunogenic cell death, promoting cytotoxic T-cell infiltration while suppressing immunosuppressive cell populations. In combination with cisplatin, CMPE effectively remodels the tumor immune microenvironment, resulting in pronounced tumor inhibition and prevention.


ABSTRACT

Chemotherapy remains a major strategy for cancer treatment, with cisplatin widely used as a first-line agent for diverse malignancies. Although cisplatin efficiently induces tumor cell death through DNA damage, its therapeutic efficacy is often limited by the development of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that restricts effective immune activation. Here, we report a rationally engineered photosensitizer, CMPE, featuring efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and precise mitochondrial targeting. Upon spatially controlled light activation, CMPE induces mitochondrial oxidative stress and, in combination with cisplatin, triggers potent immunogenic cell death accompanied by robust release of damage-associated molecular patterns that promote immune cell maturation and activation. In vivo, CMPE in combination with cisplatin enhances CD8+ T-cell infiltration while reducing immunosuppressive cell populations, thereby converting immunologically “cold” tumors into an immune-active phenotype and ultimately leading to significant tumor growth inhibition. Moreover, tumor cells pretreated with CMPE, either alone or combined with cisplatin, function as an effective whole-cell vaccine that elicits durable immune memory and suppresses tumor recurrence. These findings demonstrate that a mitochondria-targeted photosensitizer can serve as an effective platform for synergistic chemo-photodynamic immunotherapy.

item.title: An Integrated Bio‐Based Film With Dynamic Covalent Networks for Coupled pH‐Responsive Release and Colorimetric Reporting
item.description:
A pH-responsive intelligent film was prepared by constructing a dynamic Schiff base network through quaternized chitosan (HACC) and dialdehyde cellulose (DAC). This film exhibits controllable swelling and release behavior in different pH environments (4.0–9.0), and presents significant color change (yellow→reddish brown) due to the incorporation of curcumin, while also possessing enhanced mechanical properties and antioxidant activity. This study provides a new strategy for the development of bio-based packaging materials that integrate sensing, controlled release, and protective functions.


ABSTRACT

A multifunctional smart film was fabricated via dynamic Schiff base cross-linking between quaternary ammonium chitosan (HACC) and dialdehyde cellulose (DAC), enabling the integrated encapsulation, controlled release, and visual indication of curcumin within a single matrix without external sensors. Structural analyses (FTIR, XPS) confirmed the formation of the pH-responsive dynamic network. Curcumin incorporation significantly enhanced the film's performance, increasing tensile strength (TS) by ∼60%, improving barrier properties, and providing potent antioxidant activity (DPPH scavenging efficiency approaching 90%). The swelling behavior and release kinetics of the films were highly pH-dependent. Rapid burst release dominated by nonFickian diffusion was observed under acidic conditions (pH 4.0), whereas slow, sustained Fickian diffusion-controlled release occurred in neutral and alkaline environments (pH 7.0 and 9.0). Owing to the intrinsic chromophoric properties of curcumin, the films displayed distinct and reversible pH-dependent color changes, transitioning from bright yellow in acidic media to reddish-brown in alkaline conditions, enabling intuitive visual monitoring of environmental changes. This work demonstrates an effective strategy for designing bio-based innovative packaging materials that integrate sensing, protection, and controlled release functions within a unified, dynamically responsive polysaccharide network.

item.title: Skeleton‐Rearranged Prenylated Acetophenone Dimers With Anti‐Renal Fibrosis Activity From Maclurodendron oligophlebium
item.description:
Five undescribed pairs of dimeric prenylated acetophenone (PAP) enantiomers (1–5) were isolated from the ethnomedicinal plant Maclurodendron oligophlebium. Structurally, compounds 1–3 feature three unprecedented carbon skeletons. Compounds 3–5 represent the first examples of PAPs containing a primary enamine group. Biologically, some isolates exhibited significant, dose-dependent anti-fibrotic effects at noncytotoxic concentrations.


ABSTRACT

Five novel pairs of dimeric prenylated acetophenone (PAP) enantiomers, (+)- and (−)-macluphlebones A–E, were isolated from an ethanolic extract of the bark of Maclurodendron oligophlebium, a plant of ethnopharmacological importance. Their structures were elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic analyses, single-crystal x-ray diffraction, and quantum chemical nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and electronic circular dichroism (ECD) calculations. Among them, macluphlebones A–C feature three unprecedented carbon skeletons, each possessing a highly oxygenated cyclopenta[b]chromene core, while macluphlebones C–E represent the first examples of PAPs containing a primary enamine group. Putative biosynthetic pathways involving skeletal rearrangement and degradation processes are proposed to account for the formation of these unique scaffolds. Biologically, some isolates exhibited significant, dose-dependent anti-renal fibrosis effects at noncytotoxic concentrations, underscoring their potential value in antifibrotic drug research.

item.title: Amino‐Rich Microporous Organic Network Composite Membranes for Efficient Extraction of Domoic Acid From Complex Matrices
item.description:
In this research, we prepare microporous organic networks (MONs) composite membranes from MONs’ powder with different amino‑group loadings through phase‑inversion. After combination with membrane‑solid‑phase extraction and HPLC‑MS/MS technique, we develop a highly sensitive protocol for trace‑level detection of domoic acid (DA) in complex matrices. Meanwhile, theoretical calculations and XPS characterization verify the underlying interaction mechanism between the membrane and DA.


ABSTRACT

Microporous organic networks (MONs) have attracted considerable attention because of their high porosity, modifiable structure and excellent stability. However, their rigid structure makes it difficult to form membranes, leading to limited separation applications. MONs’ powder suffers from issues of dusting and severe aggregation, leading to difficulties in separation and recycling. Herein, MONs’ powder was converted into flexible and reusable membranes via phase inversion. The membranes were applied to enrich and extract domoic acid (DA, an algal toxin) from complex matrices. The adsorption performance and mechanism of three MONs membranes with different amino content were investigated and compared. The results indicate that the adsorption energy of the membranes for DA is positively correlated with the number of amino groups. Under optimized conditions, by combining syringe filter-based membrane micro-solid-phase extraction (SF-M-µSPE), with high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS), the developed method showed a low detection limit (0.5 pg mL−1), a wide linear range (1.5∼1000.0 pg mL−1, R ≥ 0.9999) and good repeatability (RSD ≤ 3.8%, n = 6). The membranes were successfully used to extract DA from seafood. There was trace DA (9.4 pg mL−1) found in oyster samples. This work demonstrates the great potential of MONs membranes in sample pretreatment.

item.title: Alkyl Chain Regulated Aggregated State Luminescence in TICT‐Type AIEgens
item.description:
Alkyl chains of different lengths endow TICT-type AIEgens with different emission wavelengths in the aggregated state.


ABSTRACT

Aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) effectively overcome the aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) limitations of traditional luminogens, enabling broad applications in sensing, bioimaging, radiation detection, and photovoltaic conversion. Among them, twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT)-type AIEgens, featuring rotatable donor–acceptor (D–A) structures, exhibit pronounced polarity-dependent luminescence, making them promising candidates for environmental and multi-stimuli-responsive functional materials. To further regulate their TICT behavior in the aggregated state, alkyl chains of different lengths were introduced into the AIEgens design. Along with the increase of alkyl chain from 4 carbons to 16 carbons, the emission wavelength of the TICT-type AIEgens redshifted significantly along with a decrease of emission intensity. This work provides a brand-new strategy to facilely regulate the luminescence properties of TICT-type AIEgens in the aggregated state.

item.title: Fabrication of Mo─N Modified Mesoporous Carbon‐Coated Carbon Nanotubes via Dual‐Template Strategy for Enhanced Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
A hard–soft template synergistic strategy is developed to construct mesoporous carbon-coated carbon nanotubes with Mo–N active sites for efficient electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution. The optimized catalyst demonstrates favorable activity and robust long-term stability in both acidic and alkaline electrolytes, establishing a practical design paradigm for advanced non-noble metal electrocatalysts.


ABSTRACT

The development of non-noble metal catalysts with high activity and stability for the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) remains highly important. This study addresses the challenge of simultaneously achieving high activity and durability by proposing a hard–soft template synergistic strategy to construct mesoporous carbon-coated carbon nanotube heterostructures. Using 3-aminophenol as the carbon and nitrogen source and phosphomolybdic acid as the metal precursor, Mo─N modified mesoporous carbon layers were in situ grown on carbon nanotube surfaces, yielding CNT@Mo3O8/NC composites. The optimized catalyst, CNT@Mo3O8/NC-0.1-2Mo, exhibited favorable HER activity in both acidic and alkaline electrolytes, requiring overpotentials of 143 and 169 mV at 10 mA cm−2, with Tafel slopes of 100.2 and 92.1 mV dec−1, respectively. It demonstrated excellent stability, with less than 5% degradation after 1000 CV cycles and 15–20 h of chronoamperometry. The enhanced performance is attributed to Mo─N─C active sites, improved mass transfer via the mesoporous structure, suppressed agglomeration through strong metal–support interactions, and enhanced electron transport via the CNT conductive network. This work provides a feasible approach for transition metal/carbon-based composite electrocatalysts.

item.title: Redox‐Tuned Oxycarbamates Enable Divergent C─N and C─C Functionalization of Indolizines Under Photoredox Catalysis With Green Light
item.description:
Nonafluoromesitylsulfonyl (Nms)-substituted oxycarbamates are introduced as redox-lowered radical precursors for green-light photoredox synthesis. Selective N─O bond cleavage generates amidyl radicals that directly aminate indolizines in DMF, whereas DMSO promotes 1,2-hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to α-amino carbon-centered radicals and C─C bond formation. Solvent choice thus unlocks divergent C─N or C─C functionalization from a single precursor platform.


ABSTRACT

Nitrogen-centered radicals (NCRs) provide direct access to C─N bonds, but their broader use remains limited by the need for strongly reducing photocatalysts, high-energy irradiation, and incomplete control over competing radical transfer pathways. Here we show that nonafluoromesitylsulfonyl (Nms)-substituted oxycarbamates represent a redox-lowered class of amidyl-radical precursors that can be activated under green light by a bichromophoric ruthenium photocatalyst. The electron-deficient sulfonyl group lowers the reduction potential of the N─O bond sufficiently to enable single-electron cleavage under mild conditions. In DMF, the resulting amidyl radicals are trapped directly by indolizines to provide C3-aminated heteroarenes. In DMSO, higher N-alkyl homologues are switched via a 1,2-hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to α-amino carbon-centered radicals, enabling C─C bond formation from the same precursor family. This solvent-gated divergence provides a unified entry to aminated and alkylated indolizines and establishes redox-tuned oxycarbamates as versatile radical precursors for long-wavelength photoredox synthesis.

item.title: Decavanadate Coordination Polymers With Transition‐Metal‐BisTris Cations for Synergistic Atmospheric CO2 Cycloaddition
item.description:
BisTris-directed assembly produces transition-metal-doped decavanadate coordination polymers with spatially separated and accessible catalytic sites. Cooperative activation by V centers, transition-metal centers, and ligand hydrogen-bond donors enables atmospheric-pressure CO2 cycloaddition with epoxides at 60°C. The Zn-containing polymer affords 98.2% yield and >99% selectivity, while maintaining structural integrity and high activity over five cycles.


ABSTRACT

Converting CO2 into cyclic carbonates through cycloaddition with epoxides is an attractive route for carbon utilization, but efficient and recyclable heterogeneous catalysts that operate under mild conditions remain desirable. Herein, five BisTris-modified decavanadate-based coordination polymers were prepared under mild acidic conditions. Compound 1 is assembled from [V10O28]6− anions, Na+ cations, and BisTris ligands, whereas isostructural compounds 2–5 incorporate Co2+, Ni2+, Cu2+, or Zn2+ centers as BisTris-chelated complex cations. Single-crystal analyses reveal that these transition-metal–BisTris units are integrated with decavanadate–sodium chains through hydrogen-bonding, electrostatic, and, in minor disordered components, Na–O coordination interactions, creating multiple accessible activation sites. In the cycloaddition of CO2 with epichlorohydrin, all catalysts afford >99% selectivity under 1 atm CO2 at 60°C, with the Zn-containing compound 5 giving the highest yield of 98.2%. Compounds 2–5 outperform the metal-free analogue 1, and control experiments with isolated BisTris–Co and decavanadate components confirm a cooperative contribution from vanadium Lewis acid sites, transition-metal centers, and BisTris hydroxyl groups. The best catalyst retains high activity over five cycles and shows broad epoxide tolerance, highlighting a modular strategy for constructing POM-based catalysts for mild CO2 fixation.

item.title: Interfacial Electric‐Field Nanoarchitectonics of a 3D FeS2/SnS2/rGO Heterostructure for Fast Sodium Storage
item.description:
A three-dimensional FeS2/SnS2/rGO heterostructure is constructed to induce built-in electric fields at heterointerfaces, enabling charge redistribution and accelerated reaction kinetics. The synergistic integration of conductive framework and interfacial regulation promotes fast Na+ transport and stable sodium storage in conversion-type anodes.


ABSTRACT

Developing high-performance FeS2-based anodes for sodium-ion batteries is impeded by sluggish kinetics, poor conductivity, and severe volume variation. Herein, we report a rationally designed FeS2/SnS2/rGO composite featuring a three-dimensional hierarchical heterostructure. In this architecture, SnS2 nanosheets are uniformly anchored on reduced graphene oxide framework, while FeS2 nanoparticles are dispersed throughout the scaffold, forming interconnected electron pathways and structural robustness. More importantly, the abundant FeS2-SnS2 heterointerfaces induce built-in electric fields that regulate charge redistribution and accelerate interfacial reaction kinetics, thereby promoting surface-dominated pseudocapacitive behavior and rapid Na+ diffusion. As a result, the FeS2/SnS2/rGO electrode delivers a high reversible capacity of 618 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1 and retains 500 mAh g−1 at 5 A g−1, together with outstanding cycling stability (536 mAh g−1 after 400 cycles at 2 A g−1 with 99.5% retention). Furthermore, full cells paired with NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 exhibit good rate capability and long-term stability. This work demonstrates that heterointerface-induced electric-field regulation is an effective strategy for accelerating reaction kinetics in conversion-type anodes.

item.title: Zn2+/Na+ Co‐Intercalation Chemistry Enabled by a Hybrid Hydrogel Electrolyte for High‐Voltage Flexible Aqueous Zinc Batteries
item.description:
Departing from the prevailing view that ZnHCF degradation arises from irreversible structural collapse, this work identifies Zn2+ entrapment induced by strong electrostatic interactions as the primary failure mechanism. By introducing Na+ co-intercalation to mitigate ion trapping, ZnHCF reversibility is markedly enhanced, enabling a flexible 1.8 V Zn//ZnHCF battery with exceptional cycling stability supported by a quasi-solid composite hydrogel.


ABSTRACT

Flexible aqueous zinc-based batteries (ZBs) are promising for wearable electronics but are hindered by low operating voltage and poor cycling stability. While zinc hexacyanoferrate (ZnHCF) represents a promising cathode candidate, its practical application is limited by rapid capacity decay. This failure is conventionally attributed to irreversible structural collapse. Herein, our findings depart from the prevailing view by demonstrating that degraded cathodes retain their structural integrity and recover capacity in specific media. We identify the primary failure mechanism as Zn2+ entrapment induced by strong electrostatic interactions, distinct from lattice dissolution. Leveraging this insight, a dual-regulation strategy is proposed utilizing Na+ co-intercalation to mitigate ion trapping and a quasi-solid composite hydrogel to suppress water activity. Consequently, a high full-cell voltage (1.8 V) Zn//ZnHCF battery is developed delivering exceptional stability over 4000 cycles. This work not only revises the fundamental understanding of ZnHCF degradation but also provides a robust pathway for high-performance aqueous energy storage.

item.title: Photochemical and Thermal Activation of a Diarylbismuth Azide
item.description:
We report the synthesis and characterization of a novel diarylbismuth azide and its divergent reactivity upon thermal or photochemical activation. These findings contribute expanding the reactivity landscape of heavy pnictogen compounds and sets the basis for further investigations.


ABSTRACT

Azides are widely employed in synthesis as convenient nitrene precursors, particularly in transition-metal chemistry, where metal–nitrene intermediates enable diverse C─H amination, aziridination, and atom-transfer processes. In stark contrast, main-group azides, especially bismuth ones, are underrepresented and have not been fully exploited as nitrene sources. Herein, we report the synthesis and full characterization of a diarylbismuth monoazide supported by a diphenylsulfone-based dianionic ligand. The complex is robust toward air, moisture, and elevated temperatures, enabling detailed photochemical and chemical studies. Ultrafast UV-pump/mid-IR-probe spectroscopy demonstrates that 266 nm excitation triggers rapid azide-to-ligand charge transfer and loss of the azide antisymmetric stretching band. FTIR-monitored trapping with t-butyl isonitrile produces a new absorption band in the heterocumulene region, suggesting the formation of a nitrene intermediate. Alternatively, Lewis-acid activation with B(C6F5)3 produces a stable adduct that undergoes thermal N2 extrusion, transmetalation, and cycloaddition to form a tetrazaborole dimer. These divergent activation pathways establish bismuth azides as viable nitrene precursors and expand the reactivity landscape of heavy p-block chemistry.

item.title: Nano MIPs (Molecularly Imprinted Polymers) Prepared From a “Frustrated” Gold Nanoparticle‐Based Pre‐Imprinting Matrix: Enhancing Binding Affinity and Selectivity
item.description:
A comparative study across ligand-stabilized gold nanoparticles and surfactant micelles reveals that molecular imprinting strongly depends on the nanoplatform used for imprinting. “Frustrated” noncovalent interactions within the monolayer on gold nanoparticle surface can be exploited to improve both the binding affinity and selectivity for multifunctional zwitterionic targets.


ABSTRACT

Molecularly imprinted polymers have broad applications in chemistry and biology. Nanomaterials differ substantially from analogous materials on the macroscopic scale. In this work, ligand-stabilized gold nanoparticles and two micelles with different surfactant structures are used as nanoplatforms for molecular imprinting. Each platform due to its unique structure strongly impacts the imprinting, to the point that the best template molecule on one platform could become the worst on another. Ligand-stabilized gold nanoparticles can be engineered to contain unsatisfied or ‘frustrated’ hydrophobic and hydrogen-bonding interactions within the monolayer, causing molecular imprinting on these particles to strongly favor templates that satisfy these interactions and to penalize those that do not, dramatically improving binding affinity and selectivity as a result. In contrast, with freely moving surfactants that rapidly optimize their interactions with the templates, micelles give more predictable results during imprinting, governed by the hydrogen-bonding abilities and hydrophobicity of the surfactant molecules. These results indicate that the unique features of each nanoplatform can be exploited to improve molecular imprinting on the nanoscale and facilitate the preparation of advanced nanomaterials with tailored molecular recognition properties.

item.title: Bioinspired Halloysite Nanotubes as a Triple‐Synergistic Buffer Layer for Highly Stable Zinc Metal Anodes
item.description:
The biomimetic kaolinite nanotube buffer layer regulates Zn2+ transport by enriching ions, promoting desolvation, and homogenizing flux, thereby enabling dendrite-free Zn deposition and suppressing parasitic reactions. This interfacial strategy delivers enhanced cycling stability and rate capability in both symmetric and full aqueous zinc metal batteries.


ABSTRACT

Aqueous zinc metal batteries suffer from sluggish desolvation kinetics and non-uniform ion flux, which synergistically induce rampant dendrite formation and detrimental side reactions. Inspired by the dynamic ion-regulation of plant roots, a bioinspired halloysite nanotube (HNT) buffer layer is designed to construct a stable, fast-ion-transport interphase, resolving the stability-conductivity trade-off of traditional coatings. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the HNT layer regulates interfacial Zn2+ via a triple-synergistic mechanism. The polar Si─O groups enrich Zn2+ to form a localized ion reservoir that eliminates concentration polarization, while strong electrostatic interactions expel coordinated water to promote desolvation and suppress hydrogen evolution. Additionally, the unique tubular architecture and charge redistribution homogenize the Zn2+ flux for dense, dendrite-free deposition. Consequently, the HNTs@Zn anode delivers exceptional stability over 2000 h at 0.25 mA cm−2/0.125 mAh cm−2 and 800 h at 10 mA cm−2/5 mAh cm−2. Furthermore, Zn||AC (AC: activated carbon) full cells achieve over 10,000 stable cycles with markedly enhanced rate capability. This bioinspired, mineral-based strategy provides a scalable and highly effective paradigm for long-lifespan aqueous metal batteries.

item.title: Synthesis of Highly Active InGaOX Solid Solution Catalysts and Their Superior Performance for CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
item.description:
A series of InGaOX solid solution catalysts with varying In/Ga ratios are synthesized via a one‑step hydrothermal method for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. Optimal Ga incorporation (In/Ga = 4/1) creates abundant CO2 adsorption capacity (207 µmol·g−1) and strong enhanced H2 adsorption/retention behavior, boosting CO2 conversion to 11.7% with a methanol STY of 0.46 g·h−1·gcat −1 at 300°C and 3.5 MPa, outperforming most In2O3‑based catalysts.


ABSTRACT

This work reports the synthesis of InGaOX solid solution catalysts with varying Ga contents via a one-step hydrothermal method, aiming to enhance the catalytic activity of indium-based catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. Comprehensive characterization using XRD, SEM, TEM, H2-TPR, CO2/H2-TPD, and XPS revealed that adjusting the Ga content modulates the crystal structure and surface morphology of the catalysts. An optimal Ga concentration effectively improves the surface redox properties, modifies the distribution of surface oxygen species and the local chemical environment, prevents excessive reduction of the catalyst, promotes the adsorption and activation of CO2, and enhances the hydrogen adsorption/retention and spillover behavior, thereby boosting overall catalytic performance. Among the prepared catalysts, the InGaOX(4/1) sample exhibited the highest activity, achieving a CO2 conversion of 11.7% with a methanol selectivity of 71%, and a space-time yield of 0.46 g·h−1·gcat −1 at 300°C and 3.5 MPa. This performance is outperforms most similar catalysts, offering a promising strategy for the low-cost preparation of highly active indium-based catalysts.

item.title: Lateral Cyano Substitution as a Tool for Tuning Negative Dielectric Anisotropy in High‐Birefringence Liquid Crystals
item.description:
ABSTRACT

A series of 10 novel liquid crystalline compounds based on oligophenyl and tolane cores bearing laterally positioned cyano groups has been designed, synthesized, and systematically investigated. The molecular architecture was tailored by varying the number and position of lateral nitrile substituents, as well as the degree of core extension and terminal functionalization, in order to elucidate structure–property relationships governing mesomorphic, optical, and dielectric behavior. The majority of the compounds exhibit exclusively nematic phases, while no smectic ordering was observed, indicating that lateral cyano substitution effectively disrupts layered packing. The introduction of cyano groups significantly enables precise control over dielectric permittivity and induces negative dielectric anisotropy, with its magnitude and phase stability being directly governed by both the number and location of nitrile substituents. At the same time, extended π-conjugated cores provide relatively high birefringence (Δn ≈ 0.24), despite the presence of strong transverse dipoles, which typically reduce optical anisotropy. Comparative analysis reveals that excessive lateral polarity destabilizes the nematic phase and narrows its temperature range, highlighting the need for a balance between dipolar interactions and molecular anisotropy. The obtained results demonstrate that lateral cyano substitution constitutes an effective strategy for tuning negative dielectric anisotropy while retaining favorable optical properties. Overall, these results identify lateral cyano substitution as a useful molecular-design strategy for developing high-birefringence nematic materials with negative dielectric anisotropy, which may serve as building blocks for future microwave/GHz-oriented liquid-crystalline mixtures.

item.title: The Radical Chemistry of 2,3‐Diguanidinopyridines: Coordination and Visible‐Light Photochemistry
item.description:
Substitution at the pyridine core of 2,3-diguanidinopyridines was used to develop novel redox-active molecules with three interconvertible redox states. They are applied as redox-active ligands in coordination chemistry. Visible-light irradiation of the pyridine N-benzylated molecules leads to photoconversion to a higher-energetic isomer.


ABSTRACT

Guanidino-functionalized aromatics (GFAs) comprise an important class of redox-active organic molecules and ligands with a variety of applications. In this work, we report the synthesis and chemistry of novel GFAs with a pyridine core functionalized in 2 and 3 positions with two guanidino groups. The two guanidino groups turn the pyridine derivative into an electron donor that can be oxidized in two potentially separated one-electron redox steps to the dicationic redox state. The redox properties and the stability of the radical monocationic redox state are tuned by the addition of further substituents at the pyridine core. The new redox-active molecules are applied as ligands in mononuclear metal complexes, leading to significant anodic shifts of the ligand redox potentials. Depending on the substitution pattern, reaction with benzylbromide leads to benzylation at the pyridine N atom or the guanidino N atom. The pyridine N-benzylated molecules are photoactive and undergo chemical reactions, initiated by visible-light induced homolytic cleavage of the N─C bond with formation of radical monocationic 2,3-diguanidinopyridine and benzyl radicals, leading to photoconversion to the higher-energetic, photostable guanidino-benzylated molecules.

item.title: Halogenating Reagent‐Triggered Annulation of Propargylic Amides With Carbon Dioxide Leading to 5‐(Halomethylene)Oxazolidine‐2,4‐diones
item.description:
An efficient and stereoselective halogenating reagent-triggered, natural light-promoted, transition metal-free cyclization of propargylic amides with CO2 afforded the corresponding exocyclic halovinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones as single E isomers. A wide substrate scope was demonstrated with a variety of aromatic and aliphatic propiolamides. The produced halovinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones could be further transformed into functional groups according to requirements.


ABSTRACT

The conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals represents a promising strategy for sustainable synthesis. Herein, we report a natural light-promoted cyclization of propargylic amides with CO2 using commonly used halogenating reagents as both the reaction promoter and halogen source to access 5-(halomethylene)oxazolidine-2,4-diones, which enables the one-pot construction of C─O, C─N, and C─X bonds. The protocol accommodates a broad range of substrates, and a variety of functional groups are well-tolerated under mild reaction conditions, providing access to functionalized oxazolidine-2,4-diones up to 92% yield as single E isomers. The mechanistic experiments reveal that the reaction may proceed along two pathways, which are the radical pathway (Path A) and the halonium pathway (Path B). The resulting 5-(halomethylene)oxazolidine-2,4-diones could be further transformed to complex molecules, highlighting the versatility.

item.title: Inclusion Complexations of Levamisole and Cocaine With Molecular Baskets. Fluorescence Displacement Assay for Detection of Cocaine and Its Adulterant Levamisole in Aqueous Media
item.description:
Levamisole is a common adulterant found in street-distributed cocaine. Molecular baskets have been shown to form stable inclusion complexes with both substances. While levamisole inserts its benzene into the basket's cavity, cocaine utilizes its bicyclic ring for encapsulation. Both drugs displace a fluorescent dye, initially occupying the basket's cavity, to produce a fluorescence signal enabling their identification.


ABSTRACT

We investigated inclusion complexation of levamisole (LEV+), a common adulterant of cocaine (COC+), with six molecular baskets 1 3− –6 18− of increasing cavity depth and anionic charge at the portal. 1H NMR and mass spectrometry showed that 1 3− to 6 18− bind to LEV+ to form binary complexes in water, with the stability increasing across the series and highest for dendritic basket 6 18− (K d = 10 µM). From 1H NMR magnetic shielding and OPLS4 calculations, we deduced that LEV+ inserts its benzene in the binding pocket of 1 3−–6 18− while the protonated heterocycle remains near the anionic portal. The stability of [LEV⊂6]17− arises from C−H…π/cation…π/π−π contacts, ion pairing, and hydrophobic effect (ΔH°< 0, ITC). Dendritic basket 6 18− was subsequently used to develop a fluorescent displacement assay (FDA) for the detection of LEV+ with alizarin red S (ALZ−) as a fluorescence reporter. LEV+ displaced the dye to generate a fluorescence response suitable for its detection in water over circa 10–300 µM range. In contrast, COC+ bound more strongly to basket 6 18−, forming binary (K d = 1 µM) and ternary complexes (1H NMR, calorimetry, and FDA). The binding mode of COC+ differs from that of LEV+, with the drug's cationic fragment occupying the basket's cavity.

item.title: Enabling Cross‐Coupling Reactivity of α‐Pentafluorosulfanyl Compounds with a Thermally Stable Organozinc α‐SF5 Reagent
item.description:
This work describes the first example of a thermally stable α-SF5 organometallic reagent, which allows for extensive downstream functionalization by allylation and acylation reactions under copper catalysis, as well as palladium-catalyzed Negishi-type cross-coupling conditions up to 96% yield. In silico analysis shines initial light on the requirements of successful turnover of the α-SF5 cross-coupling.


ABSTRACT

Herein, we report the first successful turnover of α-SF5 substrates in metal-catalyzed cross-coupling chemistry. Previously reported conditions suitable to couple CF3-derivatives under Negishi-type conditions lead to complete decomposition of the corresponding SF5 derivatives. We report the first thermally stable α-SF5 organometallic reagent, which allows for a set of catalytic key transformations, delivering the reaction products in good to excellent yields (up to 96%). This organozinc platform allows for extensive downstream functionalization by protonation, allylation and acylation reactions under copper catalysis, as well as palladium-catalyzed Negishi-type cross-coupling conditions. Connecting our experimental results to computational analysis shines first light on the parameters critical for successful turnover of α-SF5 substrates. We challenge our key hypothesis of the critical contribution of the M─C─S angle to reduce orbital overlap, promoting β-F elimination. While we found a significant contribution of a secondary S─M bond, the central component responsible for suppression of β-F elimination seems to be the steric bulk of the SF5 substituent itself. Additionally, the close proximity of the two potential energy surfaces is proposed to facilitate either reductive elimination, forming alkene π-complexes, or thermodynamically favored β-F elimination, highlighting the requirement for careful kinetic control of the reaction.

item.title: Few‐Layer MoS2–Decorated MoO2 for High‐Density Exposed Catalytic Heterointerfaces in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
item.description:
A few-layer MoS2-decorated MoO2/CNT separator coating creates high-density exposed catalytic heterointerfaces for lithium–sulfur batteries. Highly dispersed MoO2–MoS2 heterostructures on CNTs provide abundant accessible junctions, strong polysulfide anchoring, balanced adsorption, and pronounced charge redistribution. These synergistic effects accelerate intermediate conversion, promote Li2S nucleation and oxidation, suppress shuttling, and enable high capacity and durable cycling.


ABSTRACT

Lithium–sulfur batteries are severely limited by polysulfide shuttling and sluggish sulfur redox kinetics. Efficient catalysis in lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries requires not only intrinsically active catalyst materials but also catalytic interfaces with high structural exposure and electrochemical accessibility. Here, a few-layer MoS2–decorated MoO2 composite integrated with carbon nanotubes is developed as a functional separator coating with a high density of exposed catalytic heterointerfaces. In this composite, polar MoO2 strongly anchors lithium polysulfides, while highly dispersed few-layer MoS2 nanoflakes provide abundant MoO2–MoS2 heterointerfaces, accelerating polysulfide conversion. Meanwhile, the MoO2–MoS2 junction provides balanced polysulfide adsorption and pronounced charge redistribution, thereby promoting the activation and subsequent conversion of reaction intermediates. Li2S nucleation tests and in situ x-ray diffraction further verify the accelerated kinetics of polysulfide conversion and the improved reversibility of Li2S formation. As a result, Li–S cells deliver a high specific capacity of 1236 mAh g−1 at 0.2 C and retain 475 mAh g−1 after 1000 cycles at 1 C, highlighting the promise of constructing high-density exposed catalytic heterointerfaces for high-performance Li–S batteries.

item.title: Photocatalysis in Living Systems: From Photocatalytic Chemistry to Biological Applications
item.description:
Frontispiece graphics: In this Review, we summarize the recent development of major types of photocatalytic reactions in living systems and discuss their advanced biological applications that have provided insights into long-standing questions. This Review aims to establish a unified framework connecting photocatalytic chemistry, reactive intermediates, and their biological applications.


ABSTRACT

Photocatalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for driving non-native, bioorthogonal transformations in living systems with stringent optical gating and spatial restriction. By converting photon energy into single-electron transfer (SET) or energy transfer (EnT) manifolds, photocatalysts can activate silent functional handles to generate transient, highly reactive species, including nitrogen-centered radicals, nitrenes, ketenimines, carbenes, quinone methides, and reactive oxygen species, under physiologically relevant conditions. In this review, we establish an integrated chemical biology framework that unifies reactive warheads, photophysical activation modes, and spatial-reach dynamics with downstream biological functions. We systematically categorize major photocatalytic reaction manifolds according to the warheads, reaction types, and biological applications, covering aryl azide photoredox activation, carbene generation from diazirines and diazo precursors, bioorthogonal deprotections, ROS photogeneration, and in situ chemical programming. Furthermore, we evaluate how these fundamental reaction manifolds overcome long-standing biological bottlenecks in high-resolution proximity labeling, hypoxia-tolerant phototherapy, and logic-gated prodrug uncaging, as well as emerging intracellular synthesis and polymerization. Finally, we conclude with a critical outlook on photophysical dosimetry, modular targeting architectures, quantitative spatial calibration, and translational challenges, providing a clear roadmap for the rational design and execution of photocatalytic chemistry in complex living biological systems.

item.title: Synergistic Effect of RuNi Bimetallic Nanoparticles Immobilized on Ceria as Catalysts for Ammonia Borane Hydrolysis
item.description:
Ru–Ni bimetallic nanoparticles supported on CeO2 catalyze the hydrolysis of ammonia borane to produce hydrogen. When compared to the monometallic references, the bimetallic catalyst has higher catalytic activity, and its recyclability shows that it can produce hydrogen repeatedly. .


ABSTRACT

The production of hydrogen from chemical hydrides has garnered significant interest as a sustainable method for producing clean energy. The hydrolysis of ammonia borane (NH3BH3, AB) under mild reaction conditions was assessed in this work using a highly active Ru–Ni alloy catalyst supported on CeO2. As-synthesized Ru–Ni/CeO2 with different metal contents was used as a heterogeneous catalyst for the mild hydrolytic dehydrogenation of AB. At 298 K, the optimal catalyst is Ru0.5Ni1.25/CeO2, which demonstrated exceptional catalytic activity with a TOF value of 1226.0 molH2 molcatalyst−1${\mathrm{mo}}{{\mathrm{l}}_{{\mathrm{catalys}}{{\mathrm{t}}^{{\mathrm{ - 1}}}}}}$ min− 1. The calculated apparent activation energy was 37.5 kJ mol−1, which is even lower than that of the majority of noble-metal-based catalysts for AB dehydrogenation. Strong electronic interactions and synergistic effects between Ru and Ni led to the formation of a bimetallic alloy structure with increased catalytic activity when Ni was incorporated into Ru. The dispersion and stability of the nanoparticles were enhanced by CeO2’s strong metal–support interactions, and high oxygen storage capacity, which made it an efficient support. Additionally, after several catalytic cycles, the catalyst showed exceptional structural stability with little activity loss. This study demonstrates the potential of Ru–Ni/CeO2 as an economical and effective catalyst for applications involving the production of hydrogen.

item.title: Photochemical Generation and Spectroscopic Characterization of Parent 3‐Iminooxetane and 3‐Oxazoline From 3‐Azidooxetane
item.description:
Two previously uncharacterized heterocyclic imines, 3-iminooxetane and 3-oxazoline, are generated simultaneously by irradiation of 3-azidooxetane under matrix isolation conditions. The infrared spectra provide reference data for future gas-phase studies and may facilitate their search in the interstellar medium.


ABSTRACT

Simple heterocyclic imines are of potential prebiotic and astrochemical relevance, yet many parent representatives remain uncharacterized. Here, we report the photochemical formation of two C3H5NO isomers, namely 3-iminooxetane and 3-oxazoline, by irradiation of matrix-isolated 3-azidooxetane in argon at 3 K. Photolysis at 308 nm leads to efficient azide depletion and formation of both imines, which were assigned by infrared spectroscopy in combination with anharmonic quantum-chemical calculations. Deuterium-labeling experiments further support the assignments and reveal isotope shifts consistent with the proposed structures. Subsequent irradiation at 222 nm consumes both heterocycles, leading to a complex product mixture including methoxyacetonitrile, ketenimine, and formaldehyde, as well as spectral features tentatively assigned to 2-(methyleneamino)acetaldehyde. Multireference calculations support facile N2 extrusion and reveal pronounced singlet-state near-degeneracy together with a substantially stabilized lowest triplet state upon N2 separation. The comparable formation of both heterocycles, despite their different thermodynamic stabilities, indicates that product selectivity is not governed by thermodynamic stability alone.

item.title: Dilemma in Carotenoids Versus Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) Synthesis Using Haloarchaea as Cell Factories
item.description:
Production of PHAs by haloarchaea: the production of carotenoids and PHAs is concomitant, and consequently, various metabolic pathways compete for the carbon source. This results in a loss of PHA production efficiency. Efficient control of carbon source utilization (favoring certain metabolic pathways at the expense of others) is the key to the industrial-scale production of PHA using haloarchaea.


ABSTRACT

Microorganisms of the Haloferacaceae and Halobacteriaceae families (Archaea Domain) have been revealed as key players for the bioproduction of polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs), a family of natural, biodegradable polyesters produced by different types of microorganisms as intracellular carbon and energy storage reserves and stress-resistance tools. Recent works have optimized the production of high-quality PHAs using cost-efficient processes that involve even the valorization of residues from other industrial processes, which are used as raw material for haloarchaeal growth and PHA production. Considering the physicochemical properties of those biopolymers, poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate)(PHBV) is currently a target in many biotech-based processes aiming at the production of bioplastics. In this context, the haloarchaeon Haloferax mediterranei is probably the most well-examined archaeal cell factory for PHBV production, with some successful processes already described to produce significant concentrations of PHBV. However, the go-to-market haloarchaeal PHBV strategy continues to be limited by the capacity to produce quantities of PHBV sufficient to meet market demands due to several biological and technological limitations. In this perspective, risks and limitations to produce haloarcheal PHBV, as well as hot topics that may contribute to accelerating the efficient upscaling production of PHBV (in terms of cost and time), are also discussed.

item.title: From Interfacial Adsorption to Decontamination Fate: Adsorption‐Regulated Electron‐Transfer Pathways in Peroxymonosulfate‐Based Fenton‐Like System
item.description:
Adsorption acts as a vital factor governing electron transfer pathways and the fate of pollutants. Physisorption favors mediated single-electron transfer and pollutant coupling, whereas reversible chemisorption promotes direct multi-electron oxidation and mineralization. Balancing adsorption, oxidation, and desorption enables pathway-selective transformation while mitigating catalyst deactivation, byproduct accumulation, and secondary pollution in peroxymonosulfate-based Fenton-like system. These insights provide practical recommendations for regulating PMS-based ETPs toward efficient and stable wastewater treatment. .


ABSTRACT

Nonradical electron-transfer processes (ETPs) based on peroxymonosulfate (PMS) have attracted increasing attention for removing emerging contaminants from wastewater. However, these processes are strongly governed by adsorption, and the role of adsorption type in regulating electron-transfer pathways, product fate, and environmental risks remain fragmented. This review examines adsorption-regulated electron transfer in peroxymonosulfate-based system by linking physisorption and chemisorption with direct and mediated electron transfer pathways. Chemisorption promotes inner-sphere complexes, orbital coupling, and multi-electron oxidation, thereby favoring aromatic ring cleavage and deep mineralization. In contrast, non-specific physisorption tends to induce outer-sphere electron transfer, rapid desorption of single-electron oxidation intermediates, and subsequent radical coupling or polymeric deposition. An appropriate adsorption free energy window is essential to balance interfacial electron flux and catalytic turnover, whereas under- or over-adsorption may cause poor selectivity, catalyst deactivation, metal leaching, or toxic byproduct accumulation. We further discuss the collective role of catalyst electronic structure, geometric configuration and pollutant molecular properties in reshaping adsorption–electron transfer coupling. Finally, this review proposes a balanced adsorption regulation strategy, encompassing catalyst–interface modulation and pollutant-specific adsorption matching. This review provides a mechanistic basis and practical recommendations for guiding PMS-based ETPs from efficiency-oriented contaminant removal toward pathway control, risk mitigation, and environmentally responsible water treatment.

item.title: Beyond Push–Pull Chromophores: Unlocking the Synthetic Potential of Formal [2+2] CA‐RE for Quinolone Annulation
item.description:
Beyond push–pull chromophores: donor–acceptor [2+2] cycloaddition–retroelectrocyclization (CA-RE) is reprogrammed into a metal-free heteroannulation platform, enabling quinolin-4-one synthesis through intramolecular nucleophilic capture cascade.


ABSTRACT

The donor–acceptor [2+2] cycloaddition–retro-electrocyclization (CA-RE) reaction is a cornerstone of push–pull chromophore synthesis, yet its broader potential in synthetic methodology remains largely untapped. Here, we repurpose classical CA-RE chemistry as a metal-free annulation strategy by intercepting the formal CA-RE intermediate through an intramolecular nucleophilic cyclization cascade. Readily available o-aminophenyl alkynes react with in situ or ex situ generated dicyanoalkenes to afford dicyanovinyl-substituted dihydroquinolines, which are efficiently converted by sequential oxidation and dehydrogenation into structurally diverse, medicinally important quinolin-4-ones. The protocol accommodates hydrogen, alkyl, and aryl substitution patterns while retaining the operational simplicity of classical CA-RE chemistry. The resulting 4(1H)-quinolinones provide versatile intermediates for concise access to pharmacologically relevant quinolines through well-established one-step transformations. Isolation of a cyclobutene intermediate supports the involvement of the canonical CA-RE pathway prior to annulation. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated by the concise synthesis of the natural product 2-propyl-4(1H)-quinolinone. Beyond providing an efficient route to quinolin-4-ones, this work establishes classical donor–acceptor CA-RE chemistry as a versatile platform for annulation and heterocycle synthesis.

item.title: Enhanced Singlet Oxygen Production in Supramolecular Artificial Light‐Harvesting System for Photooxidation of 4‐(Methylthio)toluene
item.description:
An enhanced singlet oxygen production artificial light-harvesting system was constructed by supramolecular assembly for the photooxidation of 4-(methylthio)toluene to 4-(methylsulfinyl)toluene.


ABSTRACT

An enhanced singlet oxygen (1O2) production artificial light-harvesting systems (LHSs) was constructed by supramolecular assembly of water-soluble pillar[5]arene (WP5) and naphthylhydroxyphenyl derivative (NHD). After WP5 and NHD binding to form WP5-NHD amphiphiles, WP5-NHD complex self-assembled to WP5-NHD nanoparticles, which exhibited significantly teal aggregation-induced emission (AIE) fluorescence to serve as donors. By loading eosin Y (ESY) and sulforhodamine 101 (SR101) acceptors, two artificial LHSs of WP5-NHD-ESY and WP5-NHD-SR101 were constructed by Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) process, whose energy transfer efficiency and antenna effect were 53.8%, 15.0 and 59.7%, 21.9, respectively. Notably, through the energy transfer in WP5-NHD-SR101, UV region solar energy was efficiently absorbed by WP5-NHD and transferred to SR101 for enhancing 1O2 production. In order to mimic natural LHS's photocatalytic utilization, WP5-NHD-SR101 LHS was used as a clean-green oxidant to catalyze the photooxidation of 4-(methylthio)toluene to 4-(methylsulfinyl)toluene, whose yield was significantly improved to 62%, showing potential in solar energy transfer and utilization.

item.title: Facile Synthesis of Highly Crystalline Schiff‐Base Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Iodine Adsorption
item.description:
COF-Sptza with the high crystallinity was successfully synthesized via a green route using 4-dimethylaminopyridine (DMAP) as the flux reagent at 150°C for 24 h, which achieved a high saturated iodine adsorption capacity of 10.77 g·g−1 at 75°C under ambient pressure, making it one of the most efficient iodine adsorption COF materials for application in nuclear waste treatment.


ABSTRACT

Crystalline covalent organic framework (COF) materials have demonstrated remarkable potentials in the field of adsorption, in particular adsorption of radioactive substances with extremely environmental hazards, owing to their high specific surface area, few structural defects, and excellent stability. So far, most highly crystalline COFs including Schiff-base COFs are mainly synthesized via traditional solvothermal methods, which, however, inevitably generate waste liquid and require high reaction temperatures and prolonged reaction times with the large-scale production thus limited. The rapid and efficient synthesis of highly crystalline COFs is still a key challenge. Herein, following the 4-dimethylamino pyridine (DMAP)-mediated melt polymerization process, Schiff-base COFs were efficiently synthesized with a short reaction time, low temperature required and no pollution waste generated, resulting in different Schiff-base COF materials that exhibit high crystallinity and porosity, and large specific surface areas, as well as excellent stabilities toward both acidic and alkaline conditions. Encouragingly, the obtained Schiff-base COF materials demonstrated excellent iodine adsorption capacities with COF-Sptza achieving saturated iodine adsorption capacities of 10.77 g/g (1077.3% by mass), at 75 °C under ambient pressure, owing to their electron-rich heteroatom active sites, which makes it one of the most efficient iodine adsorption COF materials for application in nuclear waste treatment.

item.title: Metal–Organic Frameworks for Stabilizing Zinc Metal Anodes in Aqueous Batteries: Structure–Interface–Performance Relationships: A Critical Review
item.description:
Structure–interface–performance relationships for MOF-regulated aqueous Zn metal anodes are established by linking four implementation strategies with five interfacial mechanisms and their coupling and competition. Rational design requires coordinated balancing of homogeneous nucleation, selective deposition, zincophilic regulation, Zn2+ desolvation, and shielding against free water and anions to enable reversible Zn plating and stripping.


ABSTRACT

Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs), with intrinsic advantages such as environmental friendliness, cost-effectiveness, and high theoretical capacity, have emerged as promising candidates for energy storage systems. However, the zinc anode in ZIBs faces several challenges, including dendrite formation, the hydrogen evolution reaction, corrosion, and surface passivation. These processes are strongly coupled rather than independent failure modes. To address these challenges, functional-material-based strategies involving electrode architecture, interface engineering, separator modification, and electrolyte regulation have been developed to improve the reversibility of the Zn metal anode. This review summarizes a structure–interface–performance framework for understanding MOF-enabled stabilization of Zn metal anodes. Four implementation routes are systematically examined and compared: MOF protective coatings, MOF-based three-dimensional hosts, MOF-modified separators, and MOF-containing liquid, gel, or solid-state electrolytes. Particular attention is paid to the relationships between pore aperture, framework chemistry, zincophilic sites, conductivity, mechanical integrity and five major interfacial functions: homogeneous nucleation, selective deposition, zincophilic regulation, accelerating Zn2+ desolvation, and interfacial shielding against water and detrimental anions. Representative studies are critically assessed by considering the trade-offs between ion selectivity and ionic conductivity, interfacial protection and transport resistance, and long-duration laboratory cycling and practical Zn utilization, allowing to develop predictive design principles for MOF-enabled aqueous Zn metal batteries.

item.title: H‐Aggregated Cationic Isomers to Boost ROS Generation for Photodynamic Therapy
item.description:
H-aggregation provides a promising strategy to enhance reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation for photodynamic therapy. Herein, two cationic isomers, 2-IVQ and 4-IVQ, were designed to investigate aggregation-dependent photodynamic activity. Compared with 4-IVQ, 2-IVQ forms tighter H-aggregates, facilitating intersystem crossing and boosting ROS generation. Upon light irradiation, mitochondria-accumulated 2-IVQ induced oxidative damage and cancer cell apoptosis. Its subsequent translocation from mitochondria to nucleoli enabled self-reporting of the photodynamic therapeutic process. Furthermore, 2-IVQ exhibits significant antitumor efficacy in vivo, demonstrating the potential of H-aggregation-based photosensitizers for effective cancer phototheranostics.


ABSTRACT

Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has become a burgeoning alternative modality in clinics to treat cancer, and photosensitizers are the critical components for PDT. Herein, considering that the radiative transition from the S1 to S0 energy states in H-aggregates is symmetry-forbidden, we proposed that H-aggregates were more prone to undergo intersystem crossing (ISC), thereby generating a photodynamic effect. Based on this hypothesis, we have successfully designed and synthesized a pair of isomers with planar structure, 2-IVQ and 4-IVQ, to seek for an efficient sensitizer working on H-aggregation mechanism. 2-IVQ tends to form H-aggregates more readily, and the formation of H-aggregates at high concentrations actually enables effective generation of the photodynamic effect. Interestingly, at low concentrations, 2-IVQ exhibits a weaker photodynamic effect compared to 4-IVQ, which further supports the formation of H-aggregates in 2-IVQ at high concentrations. Concentrated in mitochondria of cancer cells, tightly H-aggregated 2-IVQ showed faster ROS generation that induced cell apoptosis, and could self-report entire PDT process by visualizing the dyeing position change from mitochondria to nucleolus. In addition, 2-IVQ had a substantial antitumor effect in H460 tumor bearing mice. This work provides a new strategy to promote the ISC for constructing effective phototheranostic reagents based on H-aggregation mechanism.

item.title: Engineering Cell‐Free Protein Synthesis Within Protocells
item.description:
This review highlights how diverse protocell platforms create cell-like microenvironments for compartmentalized cell-free protein synthesis and programmable gene expression. By coupling protein synthesis with genetic replication, membrane growth, morphogenesis, division, and intercellular communication, these systems enable the reconstitution of increasingly complex cellular functions, paving the way toward the bottom-up construction of life-like artificial cells.


ABSTRACT

Cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) has emerged as a versatile platform for producing proteins in vitro with exceptional programmability, rapid prototyping capability, and an open biochemical environment. However, conventional CFPS is typically performed in homogeneous solutions that lack the spatial organization, molecular confinement, and dynamic regulation characteristic of living cells. Integrating CFPS with protocells overcomes these limitations by recreating cell-like microenvironments that enable compartmentalized gene expression and increasingly life-like biological functions. In this review, we summarize recent advances in protocell platforms for CFPS and discuss how compartmentalization influences the efficiency, regulation, and functionality of protein synthesis. We compare the major protocell platforms and highlight the physicochemical principles governing confined protein synthesis, such as molecular crowding, selective permeability, molecular partitioning, and phase separation. We then review strategies for enhancing protein production and constructing life-like behaviors, including programmable gene expression, membrane protein synthesis, DNA replication, membrane growth, morphogenesis, division, and intercellular communication. Finally, we discuss emerging applications in biosensing, protein engineering, and therapeutics, and outline future challenges and opportunities for developing protein-producing protocells toward living systems.

item.title: Electronic and Steric Effects on the Photoswitching and Thermal Relaxation of Ortho‐Substituted Pyrazole Azo Phthalimides
item.description:
Ortho substitution decouples photochemical addressability from thermal persistence in pyrazole azo phthalimides. The CF3 derivative undergoes E→Z switching with green light and retains the Z state for 3 days, whereas the CH3 analogue relaxes within 112 s. Experiment and computation reveal that these effects arise from substituent-dependent reshaping of a coupled torsional, bending, and N═N bond-order landscape. .


ABSTRACT

Ortho-substituted phthalimide–azopyrazole photoswitches bearing CH3, CF3, tert-Bu, and Ph groups were developed to determine how local steric and electronic perturbations control photochemical addressability and thermal Z→E relaxation. The substituents induced substantial shifts in absorption maxima, enabling different irradiation wavelengths while producing modest differences in the attainable Z-rich photostationary states. The CF3 derivative underwent E→Z photoisomerization at 530 nm, whereas the other derivatives were switched at 370 nm. TD-DFT analysis attributes this spectral differentiation to orbital reordering, configuration mixing, and redistribution of oscillator strength within the low-energy excited-state manifold. Thermal Z→E half-lives span more than three orders of magnitude, from 112 s for the CH3 derivative to 73 h for the CF3 derivative. Eyring analysis reveals predominantly entropic differentiation among the CH3, tert-Bu, and Ph derivatives, whereas CF3 persistence is primarily enthalpic. Adiabatic S0 calculations reproduce the experimental stability order but do not account for the substantially negative experimental activation entropies. Relaxed T1 scans and optimized S0/T1 crossing points identify accessible twisted crossing regions.
